title: How Does an Electric Eel Shock Something Above the Water? It Jumps
subject: electric eel

scenes.text: An electric eel can shock things that aren't even in the water. Here's how.
In 2016, a Vanderbilt biologist showed that eels leap out of the water and press their chin against a threat.
In water, the shock spreads in every direction. Leaping sends the charge straight through the target.
The higher the eel leaps, the stronger the shock. Slow-motion video shows it bending its neck to stay in contact.
One species, discovered in 2019, was measured at about eight hundred sixty volts, the highest of any animal.
Humboldt described this in 1800. Science took two hundred sixteen years to confirm it.

description:
Electric eels leap out of the water and shock whatever they touch.
The higher they leap, the stronger the shock, and one species reached about 860 volts.
Would you reach into that river?
